_comment: Highest counts this repository is allowed to carry, and the critical/high advisory ids it carries per target. Lower both by fixing advisories and re-running `node scripts/audit-ratchet.mjs --update`; raising a count or adding an id is a deliberate edit that belongs in a commit message with a reason. A new advisory that cannot be fixed yet goes in `accepted` as { id } or { package, range } with a reason and an expires date (YYYY-MM-DD).

accepted.reason: No fixed release exists (3.0.3 is the latest). braces is reached only through http-proxy-middleware -> micromatch (server, nextcloud-connector) and nodemon (dev). The advisory needs attacker-controlled glob PATTERNS; none of our createProxyMiddleware calls (server/routes/webpagesFullTierProxy.js, nextcloud-connector/src/proxy.js, ncProxy.js) passes a pathFilter, so micromatch never expands a pattern, let alone one from a request. In mobile it is reached only through expo -> @expo/metro -> metro-file-map -> micromatch: the bundler on the build machine, never in the APK, with glob patterns from our own config. Revisit when braces publishes a fix.
accepted.reachability: Reviewed all production createProxyMiddleware calls in server/routes/webpagesFullTierProxy.js, nextcloud-connector/src/proxy.js and nextcloud-connector/src/ncProxy.js against http-proxy-middleware 4.2.0 and micromatch 4.0.8. None configures a glob pathFilter; no user-controlled pattern reaches braces. Proxy HTTP/WebSocket regression suites cover these call sites. Nodemon is development-only.

accepted.reason: No fixed release exists (1.4.0 is the latest). In mobile, node-forge is reached only through expo -> @expo/cli -> @expo/code-signing-certificates: the Expo command-line tool that runs on the build machine (expo prebuild/export, dev server). It is not imported by the app, so Metro never bundles it into the APK, and the app does not use expo-updates code signing. Revisit when node-forge publishes a fix.
accepted.reachability: npm ls in mobile/ shows node-forge 1.4.0 only under @expo/cli/@expo/code-signing-certificates; no file in mobile/src, mobile/modules or the app config imports node-forge or @expo/code-signing-certificates, and expo-updates is not a dependency. The vulnerable path (PKCS#1 v1.5 signature verification) runs only inside the CLI on a developer or CI machine, never on a user device.

accepted.reason: The fixed release (0.5.1) is ESM-only, and the only consumer, query-string 7 (a dependency of expo-router 57), loads it with require(): an npm override to 0.5.1 breaks the module load. The fix is expo-router 58 / the next Expo SDK, a major upgrade of the mobile app that is its own change. The advisory is quadratic CPU time while decoding a long run of percent-encoded bytes in a query string; the worst case is a hang of one app session after the user opens a crafted deep link, no data exposure and nothing reachable without that tap.
accepted.reachability: npm ls in mobile/ shows decode-uri-component 0.2.2 only under expo-router -> query-string. expo-router calls queryString.parse on the query of a deep link in react-navigation/core/getStateFromPath.js, so a crafted link opened on the device reaches the vulnerable code; the effect is bounded to CPU time on that device. No file in mobile/src or mobile/modules imports query-string or decode-uri-component directly.
